verdict.summary: The global payment gateway presents potential issues with data storage and user consent due to the inability to access necessary legislative information.

issues.title: Insufficient Data Storage Regulations
issues.description: The payment gateway stores personal identifiers indefinitely without clear compliance with local data retention policies.
issues.impact: Regulatory fines and loss of user trust
issues.remediation: Implement storage policies that align with local data retention requirements.

issues.title: Unclear User Consent Mechanisms
issues.description: The inability to access legislative information impacts the understanding of the gateway's user consent practices.
issues.remediation: Ensure all necessary legislative information can be accessed and that user consent mechanisms are transparent.

evidence_cited.content: The payment gateway stores personal identifiers indefinitely without clear compliance with local data retention policies.

evidence_cited.citation: Article 5(1)(a) GDPR: Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed.
evidence_cited.content: The gateway may not comply with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) regarding data retention periods.

evidence_cited.citation: CCPA Section 1798.100: A business shall collect personal information for no longer than as is reasonably necessary to achieve the specific purpose for which the personal information was collected.
evidence_cited.content: The gateway may not comply with the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) regarding data retention periods.

evidence_cited.citation: Opt-in requirement varies by jurisdiction and may be required for storing personal data indefinitely.
evidence_cited.content: The gateway's user consent mechanisms may need to meet various opt-in requirements depending on the jurisdiction.
